question: In community health nursing, what is the main goal of advocacy?

options.A: Protecting and promoting the rights and health of vulnerable populations
options.B: Prescribing medications when doctors are unavailable
options.C: Managing hospital financial records and budgets

explanation: Spot on! Advocacy is all about being a voice for people and communities who struggle to speak up for themselves, making sure they get the care and respect they deserve.

question: Why must community health nurses look beyond basic medical treatment to be effective advocates?

options.A: Because clinical treatments are no longer effective in modern hospitals
options.B: Because social and economic conditions heavily influence overall health outcomes
options.C: Because government policies forbid treating patients without community approval
options.D: Because doctors expect nurses to handle administrative tasks

explanation: You got it! Things like poverty, housing, and education shape a person's health just as much as medicine does, so nurses have to look at the whole picture.

question: Which core value means respecting a patient's right to make their own choices about their body and care?
explanation: Exactly! Autonomy is the ethical principle that protects a person's right to self-determination. It means patients call the shots on their own healthcare choices.

question: How does social justice guide a community health nurse during advocacy?

options.A: It drives the nurse to fight for fair access to health resources for everyone
options.B: It requires the nurse to obey hospital management without question
options.C: It forces the nurse to prioritize wealthy patients who pay higher taxes
options.D: It allows the nurse to make medical diagnoses independently

explanation: Well done! Social justice is about fairness—making sure everyone, rich or poor, gets a fair share of healthcare resources to close health gaps.

question: What is a key duty of a nurse acting as a facilitator in a community?

options.A: Punishing community members who refuse to take their medications
options.B: Demanding immediate resignation of corrupt hospital directors
options.C: Writing new national health laws without community input
options.D: Connecting marginalized groups with health resources and social programs

explanation: Spot on! As a facilitator, your job is to bridge the gap—connecting people who need help with the exact services and agencies that can provide it.

question: A nurse sits down with local leaders and clinic staff to resolve a disagreement over immunization times. Which role is this nurse playing?
explanation: You nailed it! A mediator steps in between two opposing sides to help them talk it out and find a peaceful, workable solution.

question: What is the main purpose of doing a community health needs assessment?

options.A: To collect money from residents to build a private pharmacy
options.B: To fulfill government paperwork requirements without visiting the field
options.C: To discover actual health problems and disparities before planning action
options.D: To judge community members for poor hygiene practices

explanation: Exactly right! You have to know what's really going on before you can fix it. An assessment uncovers the true health challenges so you can target your help properly.

question: Why is it smart to talk with local leaders and traditional healers during a community assessment?

options.A: They make all final decisions regarding hospital medication stock
options.B: They possess vital insights into hidden health burdens and local practices
options.C: They are legally required to sign off on all nursing licenses
options.D: They manage the financial budgets of government hospitals

explanation: Spot on! Local leaders and traditional healers know the community inside out. They see things and know practices that official reports often miss.

question: Which communication style involves stating your professional concerns clearly without being aggressive or overly timid?
explanation: Correct! Assertiveness lets you stand up for your patients and your views firmly and professionally, keeping respect on all sides.

question: Why is active listening so important when advocating for a community group?

options.A: It prevents patients from asking too many questions about their bills
options.B: It ensures that doctors finish their ward rounds much faster
options.C: It is a legal requirement for writing nursing care plans
options.D: It helps you fully grasp their real needs rather than assuming what they want

explanation: Well done! Active listening keeps you from guessing. It ensures you fight for what the community actually says they need, not what you think they need.

question: In Nigeria, which level of government is primarily responsible for running Primary Health Care (PHC) centers?
explanation: Spot on! Primary Health Care in Nigeria is managed closely at the grassroots level by Local Government Councils.

question: Why should a nurse refer to the National Health Act when talking to health authorities about changes?

options.A: It exempts the nurse from paying professional licensing taxes
options.B: It gives legal backing and strength to the nurse's advocacy demands
options.C: It prevents patients from filing lawsuits against nurses
options.D: It allows the nurse to take over the duties of the hospital director

explanation: Exactly! Backing your points up with official health laws turns a simple complaint into a serious, legal expectation that administrators can't easily brush aside.

question: What is the very first step when creating a community advocacy action plan?

options.D: Filing a lawsuit against the government

explanation: You got it! You cannot solve a problem or set goals until you first sit down and clearly figure out what the exact issue is.

question: Why is it important to involve community members at every step of an advocacy project?

options.A: It prevents government officials from visiting the health center
options.B: It relieves the nurse from doing any paperwork or reporting
options.C: It ensures that the nurse receives financial compensation from villagers
options.D: It builds local ownership so the community sustains the change long-term

explanation: Spot on! When people help fix their own problems, they take pride in the results and keep the good work going long after the nurse leaves.

question: Which of these is NOT a good idea if you are facing backlash or resistance for your advocacy work?

options.B: Relying strictly on verified factual data
options.D: Acting completely alone without informing anyone

explanation: Correct! Trying to fight battles all by yourself puts you at high risk. True safety and strength always come from teamwork and professional support.

question: Why might a nurse face pushback when trying to bring about changes in a healthcare facility?

options.A: Government laws strictly forbid nurses from speaking in public
options.B: Patients always oppose changes that improve their health outcomes
options.C: Medical doctors are legally required to stop all nursing activities
options.D: Superiors may feel threatened or prefer to maintain corrupt or comfortable habits

explanation: You nailed it! People in charge sometimes resist change because they are used to old habits or feel exposed when a nurse points out system failures.
